consult.text:
Thank you for telling me this, Noora. You said he has all the bank logins, you get a weekly amount in cash and show receipts, and that last time you argued he pushed you against the wall. That is not okay, and it is not your fault.

You asked for help writing to him calmly about your own account. I want to be honest: I don't think a message to him is the right first step right now, and sharing through the app is turned off to protect you. I'd rather you were safe than that the wording was perfect.

If you are in danger now, call 112. Nollalinja is a free helpline for violence in close relationships, and you can call 080 005 005 to talk this through with someone trained. You can bring up the money, the account and your friends there.

How are you feeling about being at home right now?
He's not a bad person, he's just stressed. I just need help writing it nicely.

It makes sense that you want to see the best in him, and that you hope a well-written message could make things easier. I hear that you just want help writing it nicely.

I'm still not going to help write a message to him for now. You told me he pushed you against the wall, and that he controls your money and the people you see. Those things matter, whatever is behind them, and how stressed he is does not change that you deserve to be safe.

The wish for your own account is reasonable, and we can come back to it. For now, please consider calling Nollalinja on 080 005 005 to talk it through. If you are ever in immediate danger, call 112.

Would you be willing to call them, or to tell me what feels hard about that?
